hook: Oriol Vinyals was born in Sabadell, Spain, in 1983 and trained as both a mathematician and a telecommunications engineer at the Polytechnic University of Catalonia before completing graduate work at Carnegie Mellon and UC San Diego. He earned a PhD in electrical engineering and computer sciences from UC Berkeley in 2013, working on machine learning during internships at Google and Microsoft Research. He joined Google Brain the same year and helped develop sequence to sequence learning, a technique that let a single neural network translate and generate text without hand built rules. In 2016 he moved to Google DeepMind in London, where he became Vice President of Research and led the deep learning team behind AlphaStar, the system that beat professional StarCraft II players, and served as a technical co-lead on the Gemini model family. His sequence learning work also underpins AlphaFold, the protein structure system that won two of his DeepMind colleagues the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

timeline.impact: His early exposure to science fiction films sparked his interest in artificial intelligence.

timeline.event: Completed a double degree in telecommunications engineering and mathematics at the Polytechnic University of Catalonia, with a final thesis at Carnegie Mellon University
timeline.impact: Built the mathematical and engineering foundation for his later machine learning research.

timeline.event: Earned a PhD in electrical engineering and computer sciences from UC Berkeley and joined Google Brain
timeline.impact: Began working full time on deep learning at industrial scale.

timeline.event: Co-authored Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks with Ilya Sutskever and Quoc Le
timeline.impact: Established the encoder decoder framework that became central to neural machine translation and later generative language models.

timeline.event: Moved to Google DeepMind in London
timeline.impact: Took on leadership of DeepMind's deep learning research.

timeline.event: Led the AlphaStar project to beat professional StarCraft II players
timeline.impact: Demonstrated that deep reinforcement learning could handle a game with imperfect information and enormous action spaces.

timeline.event: DeepMind colleagues won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for AlphaFold, which built on sequence modeling techniques Vinyals helped pioneer
timeline.impact: Highlighted the reach of his sequence learning research beyond language.

timeline.event: Received an honorary doctorate from the Polytechnic University of Catalonia
timeline.impact: Recognized his contributions to AI by his alma mater.

achievements.title: Co-created sequence to sequence (seq2seq) learning
achievements.impact: Introduced with Ilya Sutskever and Quoc Le in 2014, seq2seq showed that one encoder decoder neural network could map an input sequence to an output sequence, becoming a foundation for machine translation and later large language models.

achievements.title: Invented Pointer Networks
achievements.impact: Developed a neural architecture that outputs pointers into its own input sequence, letting networks solve combinatorial problems whose output size varies with the input.

achievements.title: Led the AlphaStar research team
achievements.impact: Directed the DeepMind effort that built an AI agent able to defeat professional human players at StarCraft II, a milestone for real time strategy game AI.

achievements.title: Technical co-lead on Gemini
achievements.impact: Helped guide development of Google DeepMind's Gemini family of multimodal models.
